definitions.text: The model has k=16 latent states, one carried integer z, and fixed probability tables A of shape k by k and B of shape k by vocabulary size. update(x) sets z to the smallest maximizing j of A[z,j]*B[j,x]. predict returns the smallest maximizing v of sum_j A[z,j]*B[j,v]. Parameters do not change during inference. No position counter, input buffer, external memory, or additional carried state is allowed. In the architecture contract d denotes k, not an additional embedding width; there is one update round and no feed-forward expansion.

For cost measurement, compute the update scores by elementwise multiplication followed by argmax, and compute readout scores by the length-k vector A[z,:] @ B followed by argmax. Thus update costs k+(k-1) units and readout costs k*V+(V-1) units. Perform update and readout once per token. A and B are fixed parameters, excluded from carried state; the state object contains only z. Temporary score arrays are not retained in the state object. Generalize k to the cost grid without changing these equations.

Use the supplied task-contract generators and scoring positions unchanged. Copy uses D=4 and self-fed continuation, with 2*L tokens and vocabulary 5. Recall uses V=16, n_keys=2*K, 3*K+1 tokens, and vocabulary 2*K+17. Composition uses 5*T+3 tokens and vocabulary 3*T+3, with arbitrary functions and independently shuffled tables. Binding uses values=8, two interleaved chains, 4*hops+7 tokens, and vocabulary 2*hops+11. Dyck uses vocabulary 4 and the supplied variable-length balanced-word generator; measured stream lengths are 8 at depth 2, 14–16 at depth 4, 26–32 at depth 8, and 50–64 at depth 16. There is no per-token store.

Learnability uses the architecture in D1 and only the card's count-based rule: decode training text with the current tables, count transitions and emissions, normalize, and repeat. The prover chooses initialization, handling of zero counts, passes, and batch organization in its declared RECIPE, without changing the architecture or learning rule. Use seeds 0, 1, 2, threshold 0.99, and 500 test instances per seed. Score copy per string, recall and composition per query, and dyck per sequence. Apply the identical learner and RECIPE to true examples, zero examples, and the same token sequences with randomized answers. Both controls and the supplied 1800-second, 4096-MB, single-core budget and replay requirements are mandatory.

For the finite-state information statements, a source string is a function Fin L -> Fin D. enc maps the complete source prefix to its carried state, and dec maps that state to the complete self-fed continuation. Success means equality of the entire string. This includes every deterministic mechanism with only sixteen carried states; dec includes its fixed parameters and deterministic self-fed updates. Counts divided by D^L are accuracies under the uniform source distribution.

For the recall information statement, fix any particular ordered set of K distinct keys. A value assignment is a function Fin K -> Fin V, enc is the state after storing the pairs, and dec(state,i) is the answer to key i when queried first. Average accuracy is the number of correct assignment/key combinations divided by V^K*K. Exact recall means every key is answered correctly for every assignment. The statement quantifies over all deterministic sixteen-state encoders and query decoders.

The sample-information entries use the card's declared restricted target-rule classes, supplied by the task protocol, with a uniformly drawn target and no hand-set member. For copy, recall, and composition the class is all four selectors {0,1}->{0,1}; for dyck it is all maps from the six specified nonempty depth-two stack contexts to two closers. Prior bits are zero relative to these restricted classes, not relative to a class that also learns parsing or the task protocol.

not_formalized.why: The claim conflates identifying an immediate legal closer with recovering the whole stack and leaves the quantifier behind 'Exact up to depth 4' unspecified, so choosing either interpretation would change its asserted state lower bound.

Neither 'tables hold more than 4 bits' nor 'fails' specifies an information measure, distribution, accuracy threshold, or chained-assignment sizes, so no unique testable failure statement can be frozen.

hypothesis_class.definition: All selectors s:{0,1}->{0,1}; output i is source symbol s(i), with identity selector the target.
hypothesis_class.size_justification: Two independent choices at each of two indices give four rules; a source with distinct symbols separates any distinct selectors. The protocol supplies this class but no member.

hypothesis_class.definition: Sort the two keys by token id to name ranks 0 and 1. All selectors s:{0,1}->{0,1} answer key of rank i with value of rank s(i); input order remains shuffled.
hypothesis_class.size_justification: Two choices for each rank give four rules; distinct stored values distinguish different selectors. The protocol supplies this class but no member.

hypothesis_class.definition: Every map from contexts (0),(1),(0,0),(0,1),(1,0),(1,1), listed bottom to top, to the two closing tokens.
hypothesis_class.size_justification: Each of six reachable contexts independently has two outputs, giving 64 distinct rules. The protocol supplies this class but no member.

hypothesis_class.definition: All selectors s:{0,1}->{0,1}; on tables g,f and request x the answer is f(g(s(x))), with identity selector the target.
hypothesis_class.size_justification: Two independent choices at each request give four rules; tables separating the selected arguments distinguish distinct selectors. The protocol supplies this class but no member.

limits.resources: At least 64 distinguishable carried states for exact copying of all length-three strings over four symbols; sixteen states give accuracy at most 16/64.
limits.why: Each carried state determines one complete self-fed output string, so at most sixteen distinct source strings can be reproduced.

translations.plain: There exist positive natural numbers c and C such that for all natural numbers k ≥ 1 and v ≥ 1, the token cost defined as k + (k - 1) + k*v + (v - 1) is bounded below by c*(k*v) and above by C*(k*v). This asserts that the token cost grows linearly with the product k*v.

There exist positive natural numbers c and C such that for all natural numbers n, k, v, the number of carried words (defined as a constant 1) is bounded below by c and above by C. This asserts that the constant function 1 is Θ(1).

There exist positive natural numbers c and C such that for all natural numbers n ≥ 1, k ≥ 1, and v ≥ 1, the sequence cost defined as n*(k + (k-1) + k*v + (v-1)) is bounded below by c*(n*k*v) and above by C*(n*k*v). This asserts that the sequence cost grows linearly with the product n*k*v.

For the copy task with vocabulary size D=4 and sequence length 2, train on 400 examples using random seeds 0, 1, and 2. Evaluate the trained model on 500 test instances per seed. The architecture has width d=16, one position encoding, and one update round per token. The model must achieve an average accuracy of at least 0.99 on the test instances.

For any encoder-decoder pair mapping L-length strings over an alphabet of size D (with D ≥ 1) to a 16-state machine, at most 16 distinct strings can be perfectly reconstructed. If all D^L strings are perfectly reconstructed, then D^L cannot exceed 16. Furthermore, for any sequence length l between 8 and 64 inclusive over a vocabulary of size 4, the fraction of correctly reconstructed strings under any encoder-decoder pair is at most 16/4^l and strictly less than 0.99.

For any encoder-decoder pair mapping K-length assignments over an alphabet of size V (with V ≥ 1) to a 16-state machine, if exact recall is achieved for every key and assignment, then the total number of assignments V^K cannot exceed 16. Additionally, for any sequence length K between 8 and 64 inclusive over a vocabulary of size 16, the fraction of correctly recalled key-value pairs is strictly less than 0.99. For K=64 and V=16, this fraction is at most 1/16.

The operation count for the model is given by n*(k*V + 2*k + V - 2), where n is the sequence length, k is the state width (set to d), V is the vocabulary size, and the exponent is 1. This cost formula applies for vocabulary sizes V ∈ {4, 16} and state widths k ∈ {8, 16}, with a single carried state.

The architecture uses width d=16, one position encoding, and one update round per token, with a single carried state.

For any encoder-decoder pair mapping 3-length strings over a vocabulary of size 4 to a 16-state machine, at most 16 strings can be perfectly reconstructed, and the fraction of correctly reconstructed strings is strictly less than 0.99. However, for any sequence length L less than 3 over the same vocabulary, there exists an encoder-decoder pair that perfectly reconstructs all strings.

It specifies the learning rule, random seeds, accuracy threshold, and computational budget for evaluation setup.
It defines the notation for source strings, success conditions, and accuracy calculation under uniform distribution.
It defines the notation for key-value assignments, exact recall conditions, and average accuracy calculation.
It specifies the restricted hypothesis classes and prior bits used for information-theoretic accounting, a methodological choice.
